prompt: By Grove’s framing, whose meeting is a one-to-one?

choices.text: The manager’s, since the manager calls it and runs it every week
choices.why: The manager may book it; Grove’s point is that it exists for what the report brings.

choices.text: Both equally, alternating weeks
choices.why: There is no alternation; the person’s topics come first every time.

choices.text: The team’s, as a summary of its week
choices.why: A team summary is status, which belongs elsewhere.

choices.text: The report’s
choices.why: Right: the agenda is theirs, and the manager makes room for what they bring.

prompt: Why does status not belong in a one-to-one?
hint: Where else can a ticket’s state be found?

choices.text: Talking about work in private is against most companies’ policies
choices.why: No policy forbids it; it is a question of what the meeting is uniquely good for.

choices.text: Because people lie about status in private
choices.why: Nothing suggests that; the issue is waste, not honesty.

choices.text: It has a better home in the tracker and the stand-up
choices.why: Right: the meeting is for what can be found nowhere else, and status can be found by looking.

choices.text: Status takes too long to explain and would leave no time for anything else in thirty minutes
choices.why: Length is not the reason; status crowds out the conversations with no other home.

prompt: Which reasons does the lesson give for one-to-ones drifting into status? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The manager owns the agenda by default
choices.why: Yes: the meeting follows the manager’s interests, which lean to delivery.

choices.text: Nobody prepared, and the manager fills the silence
choices.why: Yes: the easiest filler is a work question.

choices.text: Engineers prefer not to talk about themselves
choices.why: The lesson does not blame the engineers; Paula had plenty to raise once there was room.

choices.text: Status is safe for both people
choices.why: Yes: nobody has to raise anything awkward.

choices.text: Companies require written status every week
choices.why: No such requirement appears in the lesson.

prompt: Paula’s first topic, in week three, was that she was the only person who understood the reminder service. What does the lesson draw from it having waited a year?

choices.text: There had been no meeting where it fitted
choices.why: Right: the topic existed all along, and the status meeting had no room for it.

choices.text: Paula did not trust her previous manager, and would not have trusted any manager she had at the time
choices.why: The lesson attributes the silence to the meeting’s shape, not to Paula’s trust in managers in general.

choices.text: The problem had only just appeared
choices.why: It had been true for a year, which is the point.

choices.text: The reminder service was a minor concern
choices.why: Being unable to take a week off is not minor, and it is also a risk for the team.

prompt: Which is worse, by the lesson?

choices.text: A fortnightly one-to-one that always runs
choices.why: That is the better of the two, regular and reliable.

choices.text: A forty-five-minute one-to-one every two weeks with an experienced engineer on familiar work
choices.why: That is the table’s suggestion for exactly that situation.

choices.text: A weekly thirty-minute one-to-one
choices.why: That is a common and sound default.

choices.text: A weekly one-to-one cancelled every other week
choices.why: Right: it is less reliable than a fortnightly meeting that always runs, and reliability is what builds trust in it.

prompt: Match each situation with the cadence the lesson’s table suggests.
hint: Frequent signal where the person needs it.

pairs.left: a new hire in their first three months
an experienced person on familiar work

pairs.right: weekly, for the length of the plan

prompt: Renata has seven reports and meets each weekly for thirty minutes. How many hours a week is that?
Why does the lesson say hard feedback in week two is usually heard as an attack?
hint: Look at the shape over months.

choices.text: Feedback is only allowed after the first review cycle at most companies, including Caju
choices.why: No such rule appears; the reason is the relationship.

choices.text: New managers give feedback badly
choices.why: The point holds for any manager new to the relationship, however skilled.

choices.text: Week two is when people are most defensive about their work
choices.why: The lesson ties it to trust, not to a particular week of the calendar.

choices.text: The relationship cannot carry it yet
choices.why: Right: feedback in both directions becomes possible as trust builds.

prompt: Thiago offered to skip his one-to-one because he had nothing to discuss. Renata asked for ten minutes. What happened?
hint: Nothing to discuss is not always nothing.

choices.text: They ended after two minutes, as he had said there was nothing to talk about
choices.why: The lesson tells the story because something did come up.

choices.text: He complained that she had not respected his time
choices.why: Nothing like that happens in the story.

choices.text: She used the slot to ask about his tickets
choices.why: That would be status, which she avoids in one-to-ones.

choices.text: He mentioned he was struggling with on-call
choices.why: Right: the short meeting surfaced something he had not thought worth raising.

prompt: In the shared document, which topics are discussed first?
hint: Who has fewer other ways to reach whom?

choices.text: The person’s
choices.why: Right: the manager has other ways to reach the person, and the person has fewer ways to reach the manager.

choices.text: The manager’s, because they are usually more urgent
choices.why: Urgent things go to a message; the order puts the person first.

choices.text: Whichever topic was added to the document first during the week, regardless of who added it
choices.why: The order is by whose topic it is, not by when it was added.

choices.text: The actions from last time
choices.why: Actions matter, and lesson 7 is about them, but they do not open the meeting.

prompt: Renata needs to know whether calendar sync will be ready for a meeting next week. Where does the lesson say she asks?

choices.text: In “my topics” in the shared document
choices.why: That section is for feedback and context, not status.

choices.text: At the start of the one-to-one
choices.why: The meeting opens with the person’s topics, and status does not belong in it.

choices.text: In a team meeting, in front of everybody, so the whole team hears the answer
choices.why: A team meeting is not wrong for status, but the lesson’s answer is the ticket or a message.

choices.text: In the ticket or a message, the day she needs it
choices.why: Right: putting status in the one-to-one document invites the meeting to drift back.

prompt: Marcos’s section stayed empty for six weeks. What did asking about it directly reveal?

choices.text: He was content
choices.why: He said the meeting was not useful to him, which is different.

choices.text: His previous manager had used one-to-ones to go through his mistakes
choices.why: Right: he had learnt that the meeting was dangerous, and the silence was the result.

choices.text: He did not know what the document was for
choices.why: That is a common cause, but not the one he gave.

choices.text: He wanted fewer meetings
choices.why: He said nothing about frequency; it was about what the meeting had been used for.

prompt: Which of these is an action in the lesson’s sense?

choices.text: Look into the on-call rota
choices.why: No owner and no date; the lesson uses this exact line as the bad example.

choices.text: Discussed on-call, which has been hard for Thiago
choices.why: That is a note, not an action.

choices.text: Renata asks the platform team about a second rota by Friday
choices.why: Right: it has an owner, a thing to do and a date.

choices.text: On-call to be improved
choices.why: Passive, with no owner and no date.

prompt: Which private note breaks the lesson’s rule?
hint: Write as if the person might read it.

choices.text: “Seemed distracted again, third week running; ask if something is going on”
choices.why: The lesson calls this one fair: an observation and an intended action.

choices.text: “Thursdays flexible until March”
choices.why: This is the barest form of an agreed adjustment, which is what the lesson recommends.

choices.text: “Away from the 12th to the 16th”
choices.why: A family matter reduced to what changes at work, as the table suggests.

choices.text: “Probably going through a divorce, explains a lot”
choices.why: Right: speculation about somebody’s private life has no business on any page.

prompt: What does Renata tell each person, in one sentence, in the first meeting?
hint: People decide what to say by what happens to it afterwards.

choices.text: That HR will read the notes every quarter to check on progress
choices.why: Nobody else reads the document by default.

choices.text: What they write stays between them, and she will say first if it must go further
choices.why: Right: that sentence is what makes the rest of the meeting possible.

choices.text: That nothing they say will ever leave the room, under any circumstances at all
choices.why: She does not promise that, because harassment or a performance process may need to go further, and she says she will tell them first.

choices.text: That the notes will be used for their review
choices.why: Notes do become evidence later, but that is not the sentence she says, and it would shut the meeting down.

prompt: A manager’s one-to-one notes for an engineer say “all good” every week for six months. The engineer is now being considered for promotion. What is the weakness the lesson points to?

choices.text: Positive notes always count against a promotion
choices.why: Positive notes are fine; vague ones are what fail.

choices.text: The notes give the promotion case no evidence of anything specific
choices.why: Right: a case that cites six months of “doing great” is weak; specific notes are the evidence.

choices.text: The engineer should have written the notes
choices.why: The manager writes them and the engineer agrees with them.

choices.text: Notes from one-to-ones may not be used in promotion cases
choices.why: Lesson 12 uses them for exactly that.
